Report_ID: ICIQ-LUTSqol part A overall score (condition-specific quality of life), post-intervention
Title: Involuntary reflexive pelvic floor muscle training in addition to standard training versus standard training alone for women with stress urinary incontinence: a randomized controlled trial
Author: Luginbuehl et al.
Comment: Table 4 reports median with IQR expressed as a single width value (CON post 36 (14); EXP post 38 (14.5)), not as lower/upper quartile bounds, so group_*_iqr_lower/_upper were left empty. No means or SDs are reported, so an SMD cannot be computed. Higher score indicates greater impact on quality of life (worse). The Results prose reports the within-group LUTSqol part A values/p values inconsistently with Table 4 ("EXP: 38 to 38, >0.001; CON: 39 to 36, <0.001" vs table p = 0.055 and 0.007).; unsupported or insufficient statistic type
Participant type: women aged 18–70 with stress urinary incontinence (or mixed, predominantly stress)
Recruitment source: Women's Hospital, Department of Physiotherapy, Bern University Hospital, Switzerland
Outcome measurement: Median (IQR) per group at post; between-group Mann–Whitney U test
Outcome variable: ICIQ-LUTSqol part A overall score (condition-specific quality of life), post-intervention

Title: Modified Pilates as an adjunct to standard physiotherapy care for urinary incontinence: a mixed methods pilot for a randomised controlled trial
Author: Lausen
Comment: Values are pre–post CHANGE scores, not post-intervention means (the paper reports only change scores in Table 3 for this analysis). I-QOL is a higher-is-better scale and must be reverse-signed for pooling. M_diff computed as group_2_mean − group_1_mean (17.96 − 12.23) from explicitly reported means in a simple two-group between-subjects comparison. No effect size reported for the whole-sample analysis (Cohen's d reported only for SSI strata subgroups). n for SPC + MP in this row is 21 (not 22) due to missing data. Analysis used non-parametric Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney test.
domain: women's health / physiotherapy for urinary incontinence
Participant type: women aged over 18 referred for physiotherapy with stress, urge or mixed urinary incontinence
Recruitment source: Women's Health Physiotherapy Services, Colchester Hospital University NHS Foundation Trust (GP/consultant/continence nurse referrals)
Outcome measurement: Mean and SD of pre–post-test difference in I-QOL total score; higher I-QOL score indicates greater quality of life (so a larger positive change favours the arm)

Report_ID: Incontinence-related quality of life (KHQ impact of incontinence domain) at post-test (immediately after the 5-week intervention)
Title: Dynamic lumbopelvic stabilization for treatment of stress urinary incontinence in women: Controlled and randomized clinical trial
Author: de Souza Abreu N, de Castro Villas Boas B, Netto JMB, Figueiredo AA
Comment: Table 3 column headers are misaligned in the extracted text; values assigned as Control pre-test/post-test/post-90 days followed by Experimental pre-test/post-test/post-90 days, per the table title. No between-group p-value or effect size reported for the post-test timepoint (text states "no difference between groups"); the P=0.003 in the table is the group x time interaction for this domain, not a post-test contrast. M_diff not computed because these are cell means from a 2x3 repeated-measures ANOVA.
Study Environment: clinical (individual supervised physiotherapy sessions plus home exercise)
Participant type: Women aged 18+ with stress urinary incontinence (positive cough-provocation test)
Recruitment source: Public gynecological care service, Juiz de Fora, Minas Gerais, Brazil
Outcome measurement: Mean ± standard deviation of KHQ domain score per group at post-test
Outcome variable: Incontinence-related quality of life (KHQ impact of incontinence domain) at post-test (immediately after the 5-week intervention)

Report_ID: IIQ-7 (Incontinence Impact Questionnaire-7) score at 8 weeks (post-test)
Title: Effect of Combined Pallof Press and Kegels Training for Urinary Incontinence in Multigravida Women and Quality of Life
Author: Pinky Maria Jose; R.V Vijaya Kumar
Comment: No between-group statistical test is reported for IIQ-7; only within-group Wilcoxon tests (identical Z values reported for both groups, implausible). M_diff computed as group_2_mean − group_1_mean (4.66 − 4.80) from explicitly reported post-test means of a simple two-group between-subjects design. Narrative text for Table-2 states post-test SD 0.16 whereas Table-2 lists 0.61; the table value was used. Abstract states the critical value "is not significant for IIQ7", conflicting with the Results narrative claim of significant superiority. No instrument scale range stated, so scale min/max left empty.
Participant type: Multigravida women aged 30–40 years with (stress) urinary incontinence
Recruitment source: Physiotherapy clinics and houses in and around Bangalore
Outcome measurement: Post-intervention (8 weeks) group mean ± SD of IIQ-7 score; higher = worse quality of life
Outcome variable: IIQ-7 (Incontinence Impact Questionnaire-7) score at 8 weeks (post-test)
